shared_elements: upright rectangular stone slab/pillar set in the ground
low relief carving on coarse, weathered stone
schematic face-like features (paired eyes/vertical nose ridge in A; paired eye-like discs above a band in B)
stone rubble/masonry and earth around the base
justification: Both show a free-standing upright stone slab carved in shallow relief and photographed in situ among rubble, and both carry near the upper part a symmetrical pairing of rounded eye-like elements over a vertical ridge, which is the most specific correspondence. Otherwise they differ sharply: A bears a single minimal, almost accidental facial motif on an otherwise blank block, whereas B's surface is densely organised into registers of confidently modelled animals, birds and hatched bands, implying a far more elaborate carving tradition.
